A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Di4C research and contain 39 readable pages. Main sections, Appendices A–F, equations, figures and tables can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original image and language-generation experiments in Section 5, with ablations, latency measurements and generated examples in Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains the original Di4C experiments on CIFAR-10, ImageNet and OpenWebText, together with the empirical analyses in Appendix F.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same mixture model, distillation and consistency losses, auxiliary losses, control variates and iterated training. Architectures and inference procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions cover CIFAR-10 pixel diffusion, ImageNet masked image generation, OpenWebText language modeling and WebText-prompted continuation. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same CIFAR-10 sampling baselines and hybrid variant, MaskGIT-based teacher, and sdtt-6/sdtt-7 comparisons. Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main text and Appendix F.

E3.justification: Training budgets, sampling schedules, metrics and evaluation sample sizes are retained. Appendix F.3.1 corrects |S| = 1024 to |S*| = 1024; both versions already describe the same 1024-entry codebook plus a mask token, so this is a notation correction.

E4.justification: The loss-weight, control-variate and Monte Carlo sample-size ablations in Tables 4–5 are unchanged. Appendix F also retains the same latency analysis, language data-loss ablation, MAUVE analysis and qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains runtime means and standard deviations over 10 batches, and Tables 3–5 retain identical IS uncertainty reporting. No run-count, seed or statistical-estimation information changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6, experimental Figures 3–8 and generated text examples are unchanged. For example, the student's 10-step CIFAR-10 FID remains 20.64, and 4-step di4c-d ImageNet FID remains 6.57.

T1.justification: Appendix C.3 corrects the stated transition equation from q = Qq to a time-derivative equation and replaces conditioning state 0 with a. This repairs a local mathematical statement; the subsequent solution, assumptions, theorem bounds and proof arguments remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about dimensional correlations, theoretical guarantees and distillation performance. The added abstract sentence supplies code-access information rather than a new scientific contribution.

C2.justification: Interpretations of few-step benefits and hybrid-model behavior are retained. Section 7 still acknowledges the gap between theoretical one-step distillation and roughly twofold practical step reductions, and the need for architecture and hyperparameter improvements.

D1.justification: v3 adds a link to the paper's code repository, sony/di4c, in the abstract; v2 lacks this access information. Appendix F's implementation, hyperparameter, hardware and training-time disclosures otherwise remain unchanged apart from the codebook notation correction.

R1.justification: The citations, reference list and Section 6 are unchanged. Positioning relative to prior distillation methods, MaskGIT, SDTT and concurrent approaches to dimensional correlations is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract gains one code-availability sentence, and local notation is corrected, including the terminal-state subscript in Equation (4). Paragraph organization, section order and appendix structure are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 has altered label rendering and spacing, slightly changing page 2's layout while preserving its three-panel illustration and caption. Tables and experimental figures retain their content and presentation.

improvement.justification: The new code-access information and local corrections in Equation (4), Appendix C.3 and Appendix F.3.1 modestly improve usability and mathematical clarity. The method, experimental evidence and acknowledged limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
